Answer: D
Reason: The CT images show diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lungs, which is the hallmark radiological pattern of miliary tuberculosis. This finding, combined with the clinical history of high fever, malaise, elevated sedimentation rate, and lack of response to standard antibiotics, strongly supports a diagnosis of pulmonary miliary tuberculosis over other options like sarcoidosis (perilymphatic distribution) or metastases (usually larger, well-defined nodules).
